title: Gap 3: Compactness / degeneracy handling for the infimum

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (well-posed extremal problem).** Justify rigorously that
$$c_3=\inf_{T,\,p\in\operatorname{int}T}\frac{D_0(p)}{D_2(p)}$$
is a valid lower bound for all non-degenerate tetrahedra, by analyzing the noncompact configuration space.

Key points to settle:
- Reduce by homogeneity (similarity scaling leaves $D_0/D_2$ invariant) to a normalized family, but note $D_0/D_2$ is **not affine invariant**, so a single canonical tetrahedron does not suffice.
- Show that in any normalization the extremizing sequence escapes to a degenerate boundary (two vertices coalesce, $V\to0$), and that $D_2(p)$ stays bounded away from $0$ after normalization, so no nondegenerate configuration achieves a ratio below $2\sqrt2$.
- Confirm the identity $\sum_i A_i\,\operatorname{dist}(p,F_i)=3V$ (Cauchy/divergence; numerically verified) and use it to control $D_2$ in the limit.

Numerics: random + steepest-descent search drives $D_0/D_2\to 2.8284\ldots=2\sqrt2$ from above (best found $\approx 2.8306$), supporting infimum $=2\sqrt2$, **not attained**.
